clips.title: These observations will provide insights into how the
clips.text: These observations will provide insights into how the ocean influences climate change, how a warming world affects lakes, rivers, and reservoirs, and how communities can help better plan for disasters like floods. SWAT is a joint mission between NASA and France's Space Agency CNES with contributions from the UK and Canadian Space Agencies. To tell us more about this mission, we have a distinguished panel gathered here for you. To my far right over there, we have Karen St. Germain. She's NASA's Director of Earth Science. Next to her, Tim Dunn, Launch Director, NASA's Launch Services Program.

clips.title: The reason I mentioned all of that is
clips.text: The reason I mentioned all of that is because we'll actually start our science mission about six months after launch and we'll start producing products from from those mission from those from that period forward. The Nader payload products will start getting released to the public I think around launch plus nine, nine, ten months in that in that time order and we're looking towards a similar target for our new payload which is which is the Karen instrument with more I would say checked and validated products in the launch plus 14 months period.

clips.title: For mission duration of course every time we
clips.text: for mission duration of course every time we launch a mission we have a we have to specify mission duration here is 42 months of course but everything on board has been really taken care of and I can give you an example the the platform that has been designed by Talas Alignia Space is built against 10 years at least on orbit. So of course our system will not limit the lifetime of SWAT.

clips.title: It's just amazing how we're able to bring
clips.text: It's just amazing how we're able to bring all of this together, SWAT capability to all of us here on Earth. So we get to see that every day and what we do, but I just wanted to have a moment to share that with you guys. And one other personal item, I'm the Launch Director for this mission, but by far don't do it alone. I have an incredible team from LSP. But there's one individual that this will be his last LSP mission, and that's our LSP Senior Launch Director, Omar Baez. And Omar, I know you may be out there watching.

clips.title: Many thanks to the Air Force for allowing
clips.text: Many thanks to the Air Force for allowing us to use that aircraft to transport and here is SWAT unveiled in the Astro Tech facility on North Vandenberg. It's just a gorgeous spacecraft. And then after we processed on North Vandenberg, we put it back in its shipping container and brought it to South Vandenberg to Slick 4. And there it is, going into a SpaceX's payload processing facility at Slick 4. There's a great still photo of SWAT unveiled in the PPF at Slick 4. And there it is, about to be encapsulated with the payload fairings on either side.

clips.text: Okay, so here is some footage from the past. This is a couple of years ago when we rolled out Sentinel, but this is what it looked like yesterday as we rolled to the pad to get ready. We went vertical overnight, and we're sitting out on the pad getting ready. So yesterday we did also hold the Space Launch Delta 30 Launch Readiness Review, and we followed that with the Joint SpaceX NASA LRR, where we received approval from Senior NASA JPL, SpaceX, and US Space Force leadership to continue processing toward launch countdown.

clips.title: We will have a crisp picture of these
clips.text: We will have a crisp picture of these inland water bodies and how much water is there. So globally, we'll go from being able to see a couple thousand inland water bodies, lakes and reservoirs, to millions. So an enormous positive impact for those who rely on knowledge of water levels inland to manage water for everything from agriculture to human consumption. Thank you, Mike, for that question.

clips.text: Tim showed us arriving, but even well before that, we made our journey to Europe first and then spent about 14 months in Europe at the facilities of Talus, Leniya Space, actually putting together our contributions. And then as we went through a series, a long series of tests and checkouts of the satellite eventually brought that back here to the United States for a beautiful launch on a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket.
